near_term_sprints.name: WAREHOUSE_SQUARE9_REFERENCE_MATRIX_VALIDATION
near_term_sprints.objective: Prove or reject representative JBS inbound R-number, JBS outbound shipment-number, Strategic inbound BOL-number, and Strategic outbound B/L-number semantics, then prove actual historical routing/delivery for defensible cases.
near_term_sprints.cutover_relevance: Broad keyword candidates are insufficient. The expected reference convention itself must be explicit, and actual historical routing/delivery must still be proven before Warehouse parity can be closed.

near_term_sprints.name: GUI_TRUTH_FUNCTION_REPORTING_AUDIT
near_term_sprints.objective: Inventory and reconcile the active GPI Hub GUI, every operator action, and all operational reporting against authoritative backend truth; remove or hide inaccurate, contradictory, duplicative, or unnecessary AP/Warehouse surfaces before cutover.
near_term_sprints.cutover_relevance: Misleading operator state is a parity risk and becomes a parity blocker when it can cause an incorrect action or conceal failed delivery.

notes: V102 REV2 passed discovery closeout using the already-written full-scan JSON. All four broad candidate groups are present, but the shortlist showed why keyword discovery alone is not parity proof: JBS inbound has a plausible Warehouse Receipt W118250 with receipt_number 19944 but no explicit R-number semantics in the shortlist; the only Strategic inbound broad candidate is an AP Invoice; and JBS outbound has a very large broad pool. V103 therefore tightens the evidence gate. It requires expected reference semantics in persisted fields or labeled text, separates STRONG from WEAK evidence, preserves routing/BC context for surviving records, and remains fully read-only on the static isolated target. Even STRONG semantic evidence will still require actual historical SharePoint routing/delivery proof in V104. GUI truth/function/reporting audit remains queued after the Warehouse matrix is closed. No traffic cutover or Production writes are authorized.
